Sir, requested that I am Leela Singh son of Sikander Singh resident of village Kot Dharmu, Tehsil & District Mansa.

Kanchandeep Singh son of Hem Raj resident of Kot Dharmu, friend of my son Kamaldeep Singh was known to the family of above said Gurcharan Singh who took my son to the house of above mentioned Gurcharan Singh once or twice who told my son that Gurcharan uncle has connections in many departments and he has provided job to many boys, girls in some departments and my son also told me about above said Gurcharan Singh.

That my son talked with above said Gurcharan Singh with the reference of his friend Kanchandeep Singh then he told that now posts in department of Food Corporation of India will come and he will provide job to you in this department.
He has connections with higher officers in this department.
On which my son came to home and told me everything then I got agreed to talk with Gurcharan Singh to get job for my son in the above said department for his bright future.
Thereafter, my son went with above said Kanchandeep to the house of Gurcharan Singh and talked with him regarding the job
then he told that he will talk to us after discussion in the department, otherwise you consider your job as final and he will tell about the expenses to be comes on this work.
Then my son alongwith his friend returned from the house of Gurcharan Singh and told me everything after coming to home.

That in the first week of January 2020 above said Gurcharan Singh came to our home at village Kot Dharmu while he was alone and after discussion with us he told me to give Rs.7 lac in total for providing job in the department of Food Corporation, on which we have agreed to give this amount for getting job for my son and on the same day Gurcharan Singh took photo copies of educational and documents regarding identification of my son Kamaldeep Singh and told us to arrange money.

3. Contention On behalf of the petitioner

At the outset, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the matter has been compromised between the parties on the basis of compromise deed dated 6 of 8 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:002191 06.12.2021 (Annexure P-2), but the same was withdrawn on 03.02.2022 (Annexure P-3).

He further submits that in fact the petitioner has been declared proclaimed offender vide order dated 24.12.2021 and this order has been challenged vide petition No.CRM-M-50310-2024 and the same has been quashed vide order dated 13.11.2024 (Annexure P-4) passed by this Court.

Thereafter the petitioner sought anticipatory bail moving an application before the Additional Sessions Judge, Moga, which has been dismissed, despite the willingness of the petitioner to join the investigation and to co-operate with the Investigating Officer during interrogation.
Notice of motion.
On behalf of the State/complainant Mr. Naresh Kumar Ganga, Advocate has put in appearance on behalf of the complainant and has filed Power of Attorney, which is taken on record.
He admits the factum of compromise dated 06.12.2021 (Annexure P-2) and also endorsed no objection, in case the present petition is allowed and petitioner is admitted on anticipatory bail.

Mr. Jaspal Singh Guru, AAG Punjab, accepts notice on behalf of respondent/State and submits that in the light of compromise entered between the parties, the custodial interrogation is not required at this stage.

4. Analysis Be that as it may, having given a considerable thought to the submissions made hereinabove especially the fact that the admittedly the matter has already been settled and the complainant/respondent No.2 endorsed no objection in case, the petitioner is admitted on bail.
I am of the considered view that there is no valid or cogent reason to deny the bail to the present petitioner.
7 of 8 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:002191 5.
Decision

Hence, the petitioner is directed to be released on anticipatory bail subject to his joining investigation with the Investigating Officer concerned within a period of one week from today, on furnishing of personal/surety bonds to his satisfaction.
